key_insight: Turbulent energy transfer at scale ℓ can be written as a local mechanical effect of strain self-amplification and vortex stretching, with a geometric coefficient tied to a spherical fluid neighborhood’s moment of inertia.
engineering_relevance: This provides a physically grounded way to diagnose and separate forward versus inverse cascade events in turbulence models, simulations, and flow-control analyses.
method: Derived an exact real-space cascade decomposition from spherical geometry at length scale ℓ.
Split local transfer into strain self-amplification and vortex-stretching contributions.
Further decomposed transfer into longitudinal and transverse components to isolate the mechanism behind the 4/5 law.
evidence_signal: Direct numerical simulations showed the derived contribution captures dominant local transfer and forms a statistical boundary between forward- and inverse-cascade events.
watch_item: The result is exact for the idealized spherical local geometry, so applying it in complex flows may require careful interpretation of scale selection and component decomposition.
paper_title: Geometric Mechanics of Real-Space Energy Transfer in Turbulence
